findings.title: No DMARC record found for domain
findings.explanation: The domain has an SPF record but no DMARC record. SPF alone only tells receiving mail servers which servers are allowed to send mail for the domain; without DMARC there's no policy telling receiving servers what to do with messages that fail checks, and no reporting. This makes it easier for scammers to spoof emails that look like they come from this business (e.g. fake invoices to customers or staff).
findings.recommendation: Add a DMARC TXT record (e.g. starting with p=none for monitoring, then tightening to quarantine/reject) at _dmarc.acme-dental.example.com.

findings.title: Homepage missing meta description
findings.explanation: The homepage has no meta description tag. Search engines often use this text as the snippet shown under the page title in search results; without it, search engines will auto-generate a snippet which is often less compelling and can hurt click-through rates.
findings.recommendation: Add a concise, unique meta description (roughly 120-160 characters) summarizing the practice and its services.

findings.title: No sitemap.xml found
findings.explanation: There is no sitemap.xml file, which helps search engines discover and index all the pages on the site efficiently. Without it, some pages may be crawled more slowly or missed entirely.
findings.recommendation: Generate an XML sitemap and reference it in robots.txt, then submit it via Google Search Console.

findings.title: Homepage missing canonical tag
findings.explanation: No canonical URL tag was found on the homepage. Canonical tags help search engines understand the preferred URL for a page when there could be duplicate or similar versions (e.g. with/without trailing slash, http vs https), reducing the risk of duplicate content issues.
findings.recommendation: Add a self-referencing canonical link tag to the homepage and other key pages.

findings.title: Common security response headers not present
findings.explanation: The server response only shows a generic 'nginx' header with no evidence of security headers such as Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, or X-Content-Type-Options being sent. These headers add extra protection against common attacks like clickjacking and content sniffing.
findings.recommendation: Configure the web server or application to send standard security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy).

findings.title: TLS certificate valid and using modern protocol
findings.explanation: The site's TLS certificate is issued by Let's Encrypt, has 60 days remaining before expiration, and the connection uses TLS 1.3, a current and secure protocol version.
findings.recommendation: No action needed now; ensure certificate auto-renewal is configured well before the expiration date.
